content.value_statement: Responsive UI work can break across phones, tablets, and desktops. This skill guides mobile-first layouts, fluid sizing, breakpoints, touch targets, and viewport checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides mobile-first layout planning for small to large screens.
Recommends relative sizing units for flexible containers and typography.
Helps select responsive breakpoints for mobile, tablet, and desktop views.
Checks touch target needs for mobile interfaces.
Supports review of responsive image, asset, and content priority decisions.
limitations: It provides guidance, not a component library.
It does not run browser tests by itself.
It does not replace manual review on real devices.
The source references an external standards file that may not be packaged.

use_cases.title: Create a Mobile-First Page
use_cases.description: Plan layout, spacing, and breakpoints before building a new frontend view.

use_cases.title: Review a Responsive Bug
use_cases.description: Identify likely causes when a page breaks on tablet or mobile widths.

use_cases.title: Improve Product UI Coverage
use_cases.description: Check if a design supports readable content and usable controls across common viewports.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Responsive Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page goal and propose a mobile-first responsive layout plan with key breakpoints and content priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Sizing Units
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my layout requirements and recommend units for spacing, containers, typography, and images across screen sizes.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Viewport Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this responsive issue and explain likely causes, affected breakpoints, and the smallest practical fix.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Responsive Experience
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interface for mobile, tablet, and desktop behavior. Include layout, touch targets, typography, assets, and content priority.

output_examples.input: A dashboard table must work on phone, tablet, and desktop screens.
output_examples.output: The response outlines mobile stacking, tablet grouping, desktop columns, minimum touch targets, and priority fields for small screens.

output_examples.input: A marketing page hero looks crowded on mobile.
output_examples.output: The response recommends content order, smaller spacing, fluid media sizing, and breakpoint checks for the hero area.

output_examples.input: A card grid has inconsistent spacing across viewports.
output_examples.output: The response identifies container width, gap scaling, column changes, and test widths for a stable grid.

best_practices: Start with mobile content priority before expanding to larger screens.
Use relative units for layout and typography where practical.
Test key workflows at common mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on fixed desktop widths for primary layouts.
Do not hide important actions only because the screen is small.
Do not treat emulator checks as the only responsive validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and review responsive frontend behavior across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

faq.question: Does it generate complete frontend code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation, but it is primarily a responsive design and layout standards skill.

faq.question: Can it help with Tailwind breakpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. The source guidance mentions responsive utilities and Tailwind-style breakpoint decisions.

faq.question: Does it replace browser testing?
faq.answer: No. Use it with browser checks, device testing, and accessibility review.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: They should remove the parent-directory file reference or package the referenced standard inside the skill.
